policy_presence.summary: Princeton has formal AI rules in Rights, Rules, Responsibilities 2.4 and an OIT Generative AI Tools Use Policy (Aug 2026).

coursework.summary: Course-by-course: instructors set AI expectations in the syllabus; students must follow course and departmental policies.

exams.summary: No general exam permission; undergraduates may not use AI tutoring bots for quizzes or exams and must stay within instructor parameters.

ai_disclosure.summary: When AI is permitted, students must disclose its use (including rewording, paraphrasing or editing); failure to disclose is a violation.

privacy_data_entry.summary: For administrative/operational information: Internal or Confidential data only in University-licensed tools; Restricted data never; research and instructional information outside this policy.

academic_integrity.summary: Misrepresenting AI output, exceeding permitted use or not disclosing violates academic integrity.

approved_tools.summary: OIT directory: Copilot Chat and Adobe for all; other tools for faculty/sponsored users or pilots; access is not course permission.

named_ai_services.summary: Named services with per-tool eligibility and cost flags in the OIT directory.

teaching_guidance.summary: Faculty must state AI expectations in syllabi; McGraw recommends against AI detectors.

research_guidance.summary: Independent work follows department rules (Art and Archaeology: no AI for junior paper/senior thesis); research tools for faculty and sponsored users.

security_procurement.summary: Procuring a generative AI tool requires an Architecture & Security Review first.
